_note: Drafts for MiniMax voice design (POST /v1/voice_design). English voices for the three suspects. Edit freely; run Tools > Garden > Design MiniMax voices only after minimax_key.txt is in place (each design call is billed).

voices.prompt: A playful, cocky young male trickster with a light, slightly high and bright voice with a little rasp. Speaks fast and nimbly, full of energy and mischief, often with a cheeky grin you can hear; sentence endings lift upward. Boastful and quick-witted, like a monkey king who can never sit still. Clear American English.
voices.preview_text: Me? Steal your ginseng fruit? Old Monkey was in the room all evening. Ask anyone!

voices.prompt: A comic cartoon pig-monk voice in the classic Journey to the West style: a thick, rough but jolly and goofy voice (never dark or menacing), with a heavy nasal tone, drawn-out lazy vowels and little piggy grunts and snorts between phrases, slightly breathy as if a bit out of breath. Lazy, sly and greedy; when wronged he whines loudly and sulks. Warm, funny and lovable, animated-film character energy. Clear American English.
voices.preview_text: Fruit? What fruit? I never ate a thing last night. My stomach is still empty, honest!

voices.prompt: A steady, deep-voiced, honest monk sidekick in the classic Journey to the West style, gently cartoonish: low, calm and solemn, few words, speaks slowly and earnestly, loyal and serious, never jokes, with a plain, dependable big-brother warmth. Clear American English.
voices.preview_text: I stayed with the luggage all evening. Big brother went out around the second watch.
